# ADR — Generated files: never hotspot growth, bot-owned paths never amended in

## Context

`maintenance.hotspot_growth` (#4195) blocked a lane after 119 minutes of correct work because two generated OpenAPI
artifacts (84k lines, owned by the repo's sync bot) were amended in as deliverables and counted as growth.
`scripts/hotspots.sh` excluded only `linguist-generated` / `linguist-vendored` and `maintenance.hotspot.exclude_globs`.

## Decision

- `scripts/hotspots.sh` stays the one detector. A row is `generated` (and so `excluded`) for `linguist-generated`, a
  forge.yaml `maintenance.generated_paths` glob (shell pattern, `*` crosses `/`, as `exclude_globs`), or `@generated` /
  `DO NOT EDIT` in the first 5 lines of the working-tree file (no blob read). The output head carries
  `generated_paths`, also with the gate off.
- `hotspotGrowth` never counts a `generated` row.
- `applyAmendments` refuses an add-deliverable on a `generated_paths` match (a problem telling the builder to revert).
  The globs come from the plan-time hotspot facts (one config-only script call when those are missing; none on light
  lanes), so no new runner call is added.
- Refusal is keyed on `generated_paths` only: `linguist-generated` or header-marked codegen may legitimately be
  regenerated by the change, and refusing it would turn into a `conformance.unimplemented` block.

## Consequences

Repos with bot-owned artifacts list them in `maintenance.generated_paths`; the plan and implement prompts name them.
`maintenance-scan.sh` and `milestone-drift.sh` (report-only) still use `.gitattributes` only.
